findings.claim: The wave design lists T10, T12, T47 and the device parts of T26 and T49 in the release test results document with a fourth status 'out of v1 scope (user decision)'. D-381 allows only automated, manual-pending or verified, and I-018 (applied at this wave's merge per design.md line 5) requires every T01-T50 to exist as an automated test or a recorded manual check. The wave header (design.md line 8) still says the T26/T49 device parts are 'recorded as manual checks', and docs/api/defaults.md:72 calls the Android tuning a 'manual follow-up of the release test', while the carried note says 'not as manual-pending'. The final gate would fail on I-018 or the status vocabulary would be applied inconsistently.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the wave design that the 'out of v1 scope (user decision)' status is the single permitted exception to the D-381 vocabulary and to I-018 for exactly T10, T12, T47 and the device parts of T26/T49, record the matching run-level waiver of those parts of I-018, rewrite design.md line 8 to drop 'recorded as manual checks', and have wave 8 reword defaults.md:72 to the same status.

findings.claim: I-005 (Gson 2.14.0 for 'every module and the Android sample') and I-009 ('Android-only examples compile in the samples/android build') depend on the removed sample. design.md line 5 says I-001..I-021 hold at this merge, but the wave gives no replacement. The only Android-only docs example, lifecycle.md ServerService extends Service, is skipped in DocsExamplesCompileTest ('absent type android.app.Service') and has no other compile location, so I-009 cannot be met.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the carried-from-earlier-waves section that I-005 and I-009 apply without the sample, and either keep the skipped Android-only example as an explicit, recorded 'not compiled in v1' item in the release documentation or compile it against a stub android.app.Service in the root docs test.

findings.claim: D-434 cites as its reason that 'Q-3 leaves [TLS API 21 provider and certificate testing] to manual device runs'. Device runs are removed from v1 by the user decision, so the cited reason is stale. The release documentation would cite a manual device run the release says it does not do.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep D-434 verbatim in the wave design but add a carried note that its Q-3 reason is restated as 'API 21 device verification is out of v1 scope (user decision)', and make the release documentation and defaults.md use that wording.

findings.claim: The release items presuppose published modules ('every published module', 'installation coordinates', 'published POM'), but no item of any wave configures maven-publish or POM generation, and the root build has none. NaruServe-tinyhttpd declares tinyhttpd-core/-websocket without a version, so a generated POM would lack that version, and TinyHttpd (0.1.0-SNAPSHOT) has no publishing either. The README coordinates of D-379 therefore cannot resolve for a consumer and 'published module' in D-375 has no defined set.
findings.evidence: build.gradle:50-62 (versionless tinyhttpd dependency, no maven-publish); /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/build.gradle:6-7; docs/research/naruserve-v1/design/00.design.md:657,660,665; docs/api/README.md:91-98
findings.suggested_fix: Have wave 8 state which modules are published (all nine) and the publication mechanism (local or snapshot repository, or 'no remote publication in v1'), choose how the TinyHttpd dependency appears in the generated POM, and word the README coordinates and D-383 text to match.

findings.claim: D-348 requires 'a nullability annotation' on every reference-typed return and parameter of every public method of NaruServe-api. The built API uses package-level @NullMarked (api, internal, spi, routing) plus @Nullable, and has no @NonNull at all, so non-null positions carry no explicit annotation. A literal check fails hundreds of methods. It also does not say whether the public classes in the 'internal' package (documented as not part of the API contract) and enum values()/valueOf are in scope.
findings.suggested_fix: In the wave design, define the check as: the type is covered by @NullMarked on the class or package, or carries @Nullable/@NonNull. Say that synthetic/bridge methods are skipped and decide whether the 'internal' package is included. The check should flag any package without @NullMarked.

findings.claim: The D-352 keyword list (in, is, object, fun, when, val, var) leaves out Kotlin hard keywords that are legal Java identifiers: as, typealias, typeof. A check built from the list would accept public methods named like those.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the automated check use the full Kotlin hard-keyword set (adding as, typealias, typeof) while D-352 stays verbatim.

findings.claim: D-363 lists the Servlet decisions but not three things the frozen items already force. First, how the HttpAdapter bind/boundPort/stop/release lifecycle maps onto a container: RestApp.listen(int) is the only start path, runs onStart, then calls adapter.bind, so the servlet module must drive listen() from container init, report a ServerHandle port/address it does not own, and map the force-close of stop() onto completing or aborting AsyncContexts. Second, D-399 and D-052 require the raw request target (getRequestURI minus the raw context path, not the decoded getPathInfo/getServletPath) and 400 rejection on every adapter. Third, D-360 says the same routes apply while WebSocket may be unsupported under D-363 (HttpExchange.webSocket default throws UnsupportedOperationException).
findings.suggested_fix: Add these three points to the D-363 decision list: the bind-as-container-init mapping, the raw-path rule, and the status a ws route answers with when the container has no WebSocket support. Add them to docs/api/servlet.md.

findings.claim: The carried note says 'android.* stays inside the logcat module'. The frozen rule (D-385) and the build (checkClassReferences with prefix android/ on :NaruServe-logcat) forbid any compile-time android.* reference even in the logcat module; it reaches android.util.Log only by reflection.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to 'no class references android.* at compile time; the logcat module reaches android.util.Log by reflection only'.
